description: Enrich each order with the customer's loyalty tier that was valid at the moment the order was placed, using a Type-2 history table. A history row is valid for an order when valid_from <= order_ts and (valid_to IS NULL or order_ts < valid_to); valid_from is inclusive and valid_to is exclusive. Orders with no matching history row (placed before the first version) must be kept with tier_at_order = NULL. Each order must appear exactly once. Output columns: order_id (INT64), customer_id (INT64), order_ts (TIMESTAMP), amount (FLOAT64), tier_at_order (STRING). Sort by order_id.

tier.description: Loyalty tier during the validity range

valid_to.description: End of validity (exclusive, UTC); NULL for the current version

edge_cases: Order placed exactly at a version boundary belongs to the NEW version
Order older than the first history version keeps a NULL tier
Open-ended current version has valid_to NULL
Row count of the output equals row count of orders
common_failure_modes: FM2: BETWEEN valid_from AND valid_to is inclusive on both ends, so the boundary order matches both versions and is duplicated
FM1: Joining on customer_id only (or to the current version) assigns today's tier to historical orders or fans out per version
FM5: order_ts < valid_to is NULL for the open-ended row, dropping all recent orders when COALESCE/IS NULL handling is missing
